content:
Translated by Amir Ashur and Benjamin M. Outhwaite.
On the first day of the week, which is the eighth of the month of Tammuz, of the year 1391 [1080 CE] according to the system of counting which we are accustomed to using in Fustāt, Egypt, which is situated on the river Nile, we [ . . . ] assembled as a court in order to take account of what is in the [Jerusalemite] synagogue, under the control of the beadles, belonging to the Iraqi synagogue. [ . . . ]
Of which there are: five Torah scrolls, of which . . . , and the Haftarot on parchment, and a black and yellow siqlatun [fine silk] cloth, from the household of Sanā al-Dawla, on which is written: “Belonging to the synagogue of the Iraqis.” And a black-and-white siqlatun kerchief from Ḥ[alfon] . . . A green and dark blue kerchief from Abū ’l-Ḥusayn ibn Abū ’l-Bayān. An old black and white siqlatun kerchief . . . An old . . . and a fine white, fringed dabīqī [fine linen] kerchief, and a piece of brocade, Persian red, with [the name] Faraḥ written on it. And a siqlatun cloth for the pillars, and a small piece of fringed siqlatun for the haftarot, and a cover for the ark . . . And woven [meaning unclear] fabric for the ark in white and red siqlatun, and two rags of Maghrebī siqlatun, and prayer shawls for the priests, and a green curtain for the doorway. Two codices of Babylonian Targum and Bible, and a Babylonian Torah with Palestinian-Tiberian vowels, which was donated by Judah son of Moses. And a codex of the Torah, which is said to be in the handwriting of R. Se‘adya [Ga‘on], and at its end are a few pages in the handwriting of Ibn al-Aqta‘. And a codex of the Torah donated by Manṣūr ben Isr[ael] ha-Levi, and a codex of the Torah bound in three volumes with no vowels. And a fine codex of the Torah donated by Joseph al-Dhahabī’s daughter. And a bound codex [of the Bible] that was purchased from Abū Ṭāhir ibn al-Qiṭmānī. A codex of the eight books of the Prophets, donated by Ibn Ezra’s daughter, and part of the Prophets . . . [donated by] R. Samuel ben Avṭalyon, and par[t of the] eight books [of the Prophets] that was purchased from the estate of Ḥalfon ben Ibrahīm, and a bound codex of the Writings . . . written in a Maghrebī hand. And two parts in which are the four books of the Latter Prophets, translated, in an Iraqi hand . . . [donated by] Matsliaḥ ben Isaac. And a codex of the Writings, which was purchased from the estate of . . . And a codex of the Writings in an Iraqi hand and with Iraqi vowels, which was donated by the brother daughter of al-Shirajī. And three parts with the Torah, Prophets, and Writings, donated by R. Ephraim ha-Rofe‘ [“the physician”] ben Isaac—his rest be in Eden. And the Halakhot gedolot in five volumes, and the Mishnah in two different parts, and one composed of separate sections, for a total of twenty-five parts. Grillwork [lamps] with their chains. Four . . . , two or three of iron, and one of copper, with . . . on top. . . . And two small copper lamps, copper . . . , and three copper “scorpions” [hooks] for [hanging] vessels. . . . Two copper bowls and four small bowls . . . and thirty-eight open chandeliers and seventeen grillwork chandeliers. A chandelier with three rods and a star, and the chandelier is large. A large chain with a “scorpion,” with three chandeliers in its hooks, donated by Zara‘a—whose rest be in Eden. An iron triangle [tripod to hold a lamp] and a large copper circle—and it is not clear if it belongs to the Jerusalemites or the Iraqis. A pair of chairs—one large and one small. An ark for a Torah [scroll] . . . and one shofar, and one . . .

Translation by Dora Zsom
On Thursday the 18th of Iyar in the year 1386 according to the Era of Documents [1075], we came before the court and took an oath from Ephraim ibn Bashād—who is in the Palestinian synagogue, and who has accepted upon himself in court to be in the synagogue night and day together with his boys and to take care of all of its matters, small and great, and [who has undertaken] the service of Israel and is in compliance with them, with the women and with men—that he shall receive what the servant preceding him received, and that is [the following]: two settlements each year and the whole tax [i.e., the jizya]; and what comes after these is due to him by way of piety.
And what he receives: Torah scrolls in their cases—of these, three are copper holders—eighteen scrolls altogether, some of which belong to [the synagogue of] Dammuh and [that of] the Iraqis and [that of the city of] Tatay. Of the codices, twenty-eight are bound—these are detailed elsewhere. Of the candlesticks, fifty-one, big and small. Of the big mats, thirty-eight, and of the carpets and the . . .: twenty-five, and a pair of mats that cover the place of prayer, and a prayer shawl, and a pair of curtains for the gate of the sanctuary, and four coverings for the scrolls, and thirty copper candlesticks, and many chains that are not counted—copper and iron—and two codices for the orphans.

Friedman #13
 

By the name of our Creator. May we build and prosper.
On the first day of the week, which is the twenty-second day of the month Tevet, in the third year of the sabbatical cycle, which is year four thousand, eight
hundre[d and] twelve A.M., in the city of Ramle, which is adjacent to Lod, in the territory of the Judeans. Thus happened: Marwān b. Toviah
[had divorced(?) Sarwa] daughter of Mevorakh some time ago and then desired to take her back as his wife, as in former days. And he declared intentionally, willingly,
[of] his ow[n choice], and voluntarily to Sarwa daughter of Mevorakh: "Be my wife according to the law of the Jews. I will nourish, provide for, esteem, honor,
[clothe and cover] you, in the manner of Jewish men, who nourish, provide for, esteem honor, clothe and cover their wives,
the respe[ctable daughters of Israel]." This Sarwa daughter of Mevorakh consented and became the wife of Marwān b. Toviah, as he had desired and requested her.
[And she took upon] hers[elf] to honor and attend him in purity and cleanness, in the manner of all respectable daughters of Israel. The marriage gift (qiddushin) which which he betrothed (qiddesh) her
[is seven dinars.] Of them the advanced mohar is two dinars, and there remain for her, incumbent upon him, the security of the ketubba, five dinars, a strong and firm debt.
[These are what t]his bride [brought in] to her husband’s home: a pair of earrings —1 din.; two pairs of bangles; (one) hammered work and (one) manfūkh, silver; a silver kohl stick; and two rings
[…] 2 din.; two wraps, unbleached and bleached —3 din.; a black gown of Susa material —1 din.; an unbleached gown and a slip —1 din.;
[…] three ʿaqabiyya, a band and a white wimple —2 din.; three cushions, a wimple, and a delicate kerchief —1 din.; //a Ṭabari pad —1/3 din.// a white gown of Susa material
[…] and a mortar —3 din. The total that this bride brought in to her husband’s house is 17 1/3 //dinars//. Willingly this
[Sarwa appointed] Yosef ha-Levi b. Khalaf as her agent, as witnessed by two witnesses who kne[w her. And] with this understanding,
the two sides [consent]ed and instructed the scribe to write and the signatories to sing. And we performed a qinyan with […] with an implement 
[suitable] for doing so. And we wrote and signed so that it be between them as a title of rights and as proof. In good order.
[She]lomo ha-Kohen b. Yefet, (his) t(estimony) w(ritten) b(y his) i(instructions). Yosef ha-Levi b. Yitzḥaq, (his) t(estimony) w(ritten) b(y his) i(instructions). Yefe[t…]
[ʿA]mram b. Mevasser (may his) e(nd be) g(ood). Yefet b. Mawhūb (who) r(ests in) [Eden]. Yeshūʿa b. Yitz[ḥaq].
Ḥasan b. Zakharia  (who) r(ests in) E(den).
Yehoshūʿa ha-ḥazzan b. rabbi ʿEli ha-ḥaver (whose) s(oul is at) r(est).

source: Mordechai Akiva Friedman, Jewish Marriage in Palestine: A Cairo Geniza Study (1980), vol. 2 (The Ketubba Texts).

By Your name, our Creator. Groom and bride. May they build and prosper.
On the second day of the week, which is the third day of the month of Nisan, of the year 4841
A.M., in the city of Ṣā, which is located on the Nile, was written this
marriage deed, before us, we the undersigned witnesses. De[clared]
ʿAllūn, the groom, b. Daniel [whose] s[oul is at] r[est] intentionally, voluntarily, and of his own choice,
not coerced, not enticed, and not intoxicated, to marry ʿAzūz, the bride, the divorcée,
daughter of Joseph [whose] s[oul is at] r[est], with the intention that he will nourish, provide for, clothe, and cover her, in the manner of
Jewish men. And this ʿAzūz, the bride, the divorcée, daughter of Joseph [whose] s[oul is at] r[est] harkened to him [accepted his proposal]
and consented, with her full will, to be married to him, with the intention that she will attend him
and serve [“stand before”] him, in the manner of respectable wives, who esteem and attend their husbands
in purity and cleanness. And after he gave her 100 zuz, which the sages fixed for her, they agreed,
groom and bride, that the total mohar be twelve full, good dinars:
two dinars the advanced payment—this bride has received them; and there remain incumbent upon the groom
[t]‌en dinars, delayed, a [strong and firm de]bt. These are what [this bri]de
brought in from the Merciful [and from the house of her fathers:] . . .—one dinar, two pillows—
tw[o din.]. . . pillows—one dinar, a cover—one dinar.
The total of what this bride brought in to her husband’s house is five and one third dinars and the ten
dinars, delayed. And this groom undertook the safekeeping of this dowry and the security
of this marria[ge] deed and the stipulations of [the Torah] and the ketubba stipulations. And with this understan[ding, they agreed,]
gr[oom] and bride, and they gave permission [to the witnesses] to testify. And we performed a qinyan with [ . . . for all]
that is written and specified above [in] this marria[ge deed], af[ter it had been read to them [?] . . . ]
Moses b. Japheth [whose] s[oul is at] r[est]. Is[aac] b. Yeshuʿa
Amram b. Joseph r[emembered] for [good]. Samuel b. . . .
Bi[shr] ha-Levi b. Ḥalf[on].

ומה דאתותר מן נדונייתה לתרין חלקין בשוה פולגא יזכה בו בעלה
ופולגא יחזור לבית אבהתה ואית הוא תניי ממון קיים והודה
מנצור חתנא דנן דאשתותף ואתמרק כל מ[ה] שכתוב ומפרש
לעילא ואמר עלי למגבי בן מני ובין מן ירותיי דקיימין מן בתריי
וכל דברין דאנה קני ועתיד למקני בין מקרקעין ובין מטלטלין
יהוון אחריין וערבין לפרעון כתובתה הדה ואתנון ביניהון על
עסק שנתא ורחמותא וחייא ומיתות וכל תנאי בית דין מן ראש
ועד סוף ועוד התנו ביניהם שתהיא חטייה שוכנת בצור שנים
עשר חודש ואחר כך יעתיקה למדינת עכו בלי איחור ובלי עיכוב
ותוב התנו ביניהם אם יזדמן למ נתן אביה הליכה לעכו אחר
הליכת בתו חטייה יהיא שוכן בדירה הזאת אם הוא לבדו אשתו
עימו וילדיו אם להתאריח ואם שכונה כל חיו כי על מנת כן נתנה לבתו
חטייה והתנה עליה תניי זה וקיבלו מנצור בעלה על עצמו בלי סירוב
ובלי עימעום וקבלון עליהון תרתי אופייה אחריות וחומר שטר
הדן כחוזק וכחומר כל האשטרות המעולות והמוחזקות בבית דין
דלא כאסמאכתא ודלא כטופסי דשטרי ועל הדן דעתא חסלון
ורצון תרתי אופייה דלא אניסין ודלא כניסין ואמרון לכתובא
דיכתוב ולשהדייה דישהדון וקנינא מנהון קנין גמור וחמור
במנא דכקר למקניא ביה על כל מה דכתיב ומפרש לעילא קים
ונכון ומחוזק שטר פרנא הדן בכל אתר דיפוק ויתקרי בין
בדיניהון דמרינן רבני ובין בנימוסי אומי עלמא יבן ויצליח אקוליתוס
הניירות שלש כתוב על חיבור אללכסונן בשני מקומות אמת ונכ[ון]

ומפרנס ומוקר לכשתיעול לביתיה וקבילת עלה סתונה דא בת

On the first day of the week, which is the eleventh day of the month Tamuz, year four
thousand, seven hundred and sixty-seven A.M., which is year one thousand, three
hundred and eighteen, of the era by which we are accustomed to count in Fustat, Egypt,
which is situated on the Nile river, Israel b. Daniel betrothed Sittūna, the virgin,
who is of age, daughter of David, represented by her father David b. Abraham, after his
agency had been verified by two witnesses—namely David b. R. Shemaʿya the elder and Khalaf b.
Abraham—with a qinyan [to affirm] that she had consented to his agency to give her in marriage to this Israel. And the witnesses
were acquainted with her. The betrothal is for qiddush with a marriage gift of 250
good, fully weighed dinars. At the time of her betrothal [qiddush], he gave her 100 dinars, which is
the total advanced payment. There remain [as a debt] incumbent upon him 150 good, fully weighed dinars,
which is the total delayed payment. And this Israel b. Daniel undertook to nourish her,
to maintain and esteem [her], when she enters his home. And she undertook, this Sittūna daughter of
David, to attend him in purity and cleanness, after she enters the marriage chamber.
With this understanding, the two sides agreed, Israel, the betrothed, b. Daniel
and David, the agent, b. Abraham. And this Israel gave to David, his father-in-law,
the agent, in our presence, 100 dinars, the advanced mohar, and the rings with which he effected
the qiddushin. This David, the agent, b. Abraham, received them
in our presence. And the two of them instructed the scribe to write and the witnesses to testify.
We performed a complete and strict qinyan with them, with the consent of both of them, with a proper implement
for performing it. Strong and valid. Jepthah ha-Kohen b. Toviah.
Samuel b. Ḥanokh [whose] s[oul is at] r[est]. Neḥuma b. Wahb.
Muʿammar, the scribe, b. Isaac [whose] s[oul is at] r[est].

[On] the fifth [day] of the week, 9 days in the month Adar I, year 3 of the sabbatical cycle, an intercalated year, which is year 4,693
A.M. in Damascus, Baqa b. Moses, known as Abū Kāmil, gave the ring of security for Maymūna,
the virgin, daughter of Ḥasan, known as Ḥushim, according to the custom of the small synagogue, of the Babylonians. They fixed the mohar between them
as thirty-five pieces of gold [dinars]: twenty-five, the mohar for virgins, and the rest an addition for mohar. He has already
written for her [a writ granting] one of four portions of the house which he owns in the compound known as the compound of Zeʿora, in the street of the sons of Jere[miah]
all of these[?]‌, inside of the eastern gate. In this house there are ground-level and second-story apartments [rooms]. Its boundaries are: to the south, the rooms of the sons of
Jeremiah; to the east, the public thoroughfare; to the north, its gate opens to the compound of Zeʿora; and to the west,
the trash pile of the courtyard. This part, one fourth of the compound, is [conveyed] with all its needs, exposed and concealed,
[en]tering and exiting. This Baqa gave \\wrote// it to Maymūna, his betrothed, at [a value of] thirty-five pieces of gold. And it is the security for her mohar.
Ḥasan, [her] father, accepted for her this ring of security. [And h]e will provide for her needs until the time of her marriage to her husband. Valid
is this writ of betrothal. May they build and prosper. Elkanah[?]‌ b. Moses b. Benjamin ha-Kohen.

On the fifth day [of the week], twenty-eight days in the month of Adar II, year 3 of the sabbatical cycle, which is year 4 thousand, six hu[ndred]
and ninety-three A.M., in Damascus, Eli b. Wuhayb married Hiba, the virgin, daughter of Jonah, and gave [to her]
as mohar a choker and a pair of gold zaylaʿ ornaments—5 din. And there remain incumbent upon him twenty dinars,
the balance of the mohar. She brought in from her father’s house: a pair of gold bracelets—30 din.,
a shiny coat—5 din., a colored coat—3 din., a coat—all of it [?]‌ [ . . . ]
. . . a shiny . . .—. din., an unpatterned kerchief—3 din., a col[ored] coat,
four shirts—4 din., two covers—5 din., colored “bathing clothes”[?]—[.] din.,
a rashīdī slip—2 din., a veil, a wimple and five kerchiefs—[.] din.,
a Maisani [from the district of Maisān, in southern Iraq—Ed.] container with all its needs—twenty din., a flyswatter—15 din., a ra[shīdī] container—
25 din., two brocade bed covers—8 din., 6 velvet covers [?]—10 din., 10 pillows [. . .]
7 din., 2 curtains—6 din., a stand, an oven, a basin, two pails,
a dyeing vessel, a pitcher, a lamp, a cooler, 11 cups, 11 jugs, a serving-tr[ay]
all of them copper—40 din., a ẓarāʾif container—15 din., 4 chests—
8 din., 4 racks for slips—4 din., a box—2 din. [She] also brought in
from her father’s house an apartment [house] which has two rooms, one ground level and one middle level,
in the compound of Ibn Armīnī[?], in the eastern part of the compound. Their boundaries: to the south, [her] father’s rooms,
to the east, the rooms of Aaron b. Naḥmī; to the north, the room of Ibn Lwrʾ[?]; and to the west
the gate of the compound and the public thoroughfare. These rooms are [conveyed] with every right which they possess, exposed and con[cealed].
These[?] [that] she brought in are 3 portions from 8 portions, the boundaries of which are set forth in this writ, mixed not divided. They are
her mohar and dowry: two hundred and sixty-two dinars, excluding these portions. May they build and prosper.
He added for her a sum of fifteen dinars a gift for mohar. Isaac b. Samuel b. Ni[hmi].
Nissin b. Savoy, witness, testified. Joshua b. Sulḥ,
whose soul is at rest, witness. Ezra b. Samuel b. Ezra testified to
the acknowledgement of Eli the groom to all this in this wr[it], on the date given within. Aaron b.
[Ben]jamin b. Nihmi, witness. Bishr b. Khalaf ha-Kohen witness[ed].
[Ab]raham b. ʿUthman, witness. Ḥasan b. ʿImrān was a witness. And this was on the day of gathering.
[Isaa]c b. Jacob, the Kohen and the scribe, witness.

of her father totals 456 1/3 dinars. They agreed and fixed between themselves—this master Saʿīd, the groom,


and this Malīḥa, his wife—the stipulations of the marriage contract, as the law of Moses and the Jews: If this Saʿīd, the groom, hates this Malīḥa does not desire her, and wants to separate 


from her, he shall pay her all that is written and specified in this marriage contract completely. And if this Malīḥa hates this Saʿīd, her husband, and desires to leave 


his home, she shall lose her ketubba money, and she shall not take anything except that which she brought in from the house of her fathers alone; and she shall go out with the authorization of the court and with the consent of

our masters, the sages. "And if you are taken captive among the gentiles, I will ransom you with my possessions, exclusive of your ketubba money, and I will take you back as my wife, as at first. And I (will) have
no right to wrong you concerning all of this." And if this Saʿīd goes to his eternal home before this Malīḥa, his wife: "Male children whichI may have by you (they)
shall inherit your ketubba money, beyond their portions with their male siblings, if I have (sons) from another wife. And if you have female children by me, they shall
be sustained from my property until they are married to J[ewish] men. [And you shall dwell in my house and be supported from my estate for the duration of your widowhood, until you desire]
to be [ma]rried to another man [..."]

content:
side a
If the agent wants to write a marriage contract for him who sent him, to secure
the marriage with the woman whom he took for his sender with the power of attorney which is
in his possession, he writes the marriage contract according to this form. On day X
of the week, in month X, of year such and such of the era of documents: There came
before us sound and validated testimony that X b. Y
had performed a complete stringent qinyan, with an implement fit for doing so,
(to affirm) that he had appointed X b. Y as agent to betroth for him 
(Miss) X daughter of Y; and that whatever he stipulates as an obligation upon him and whatever he undertakes
as stipulations, he takes upon himself. He has made his jurisdiction like his (own) jurisdiction.
And this X may not say to him, to this X, his agent, "For (my) benefit
I sent you and not for (my) detriment." And whatever he undertakes as stipulations
and the advanced and delayed marriage payments are accepted by him. Following
this, X the agent said, intentionally, voluntarily,
and willingly, not coerced, not enticed, and not
intoxicated, rather, wholeheartedly, and with full senses, (that he desired)
to betroth X daughter of Y. And thus did he say to her, "Be to X
b. Y betrothed (mequddeshet) as wife. And he shall sustain, provide for,
clothe, and esteem you, in the manner of Jewish
men, who serve, nourish, provide for, clothe, esteem,
side b
and honor their wives faithfully." And this (Miss) X listened to him (accepted the proposal)
and willingly consented to be married to X b. Y, with the intention that she will
serve, attend, esteem and honor him, in the manner of
decent wives, the daughters of Israel, who esteem, honor,
attend, and serve their husbands, faithfully, in purity
and cleanness. Since this (miss) X has reached her majority, has attained puberty
and is in her own jurisdiction, she willingly appointed for herself
X b. Y, as her agent to receive her betrothal money
from X b. Y, who sent by way of X b. Y, his messenger.
And she consented to all that he does in her affair and stipulates on her behalf and as an obligation upon her.
And two witnesses who are acquainted with her performed a qinyan with her for (affirming) this. The mohar
which they fixed between themselves is so much. There remains incumbent upon him so much as delayed payment,
(and) twenty-five zuz which are due her, and that which remains (as) the additional gift,
a debt. And this is what this bride brought in from her paternal home: articles of
gold worth so much, likewise articles of silver, likewise articles of copper,
and likewise clothing. And X, the agent of X, undertook that
the security for this marriage contract is undertaken by X, who sent him, and by
his heir after him, against all the best (and) choice property, possessions and monies that he
has under the heavens, indoors and outdoors, whether from real estate
or movables, even from the shirt off his back.
side c
not like promises nor like formularies, rather according to stringencies of all documents
validated in court. And we performed a qinyan with X b. Y, the messenger, for all
that is written and specified above, with an implement fit for doing so. 
Strong, firm, and valid. And they sign.

source: Mordechai Akiva Friedman, Jewish Marriage in Palestine: A Cairo Geniza Study (1980), vol. 2 (The Ketubba Texts).

verso
Ḥalfōn b. Aaron  
Ghāliya daughter of Musāfir  

recto
By the name of our Creator. May they build and prosper.
On the fifth day (of the week), the seventh day of the month of Elul, which is four thousand,  
eight hundred and thirty-nine years [A.]M., this marriage contract [was written]
in the city of Tyre, which is on the coast of the [great] sea. [Ḥalfōn b.  Aa]ron, (whose) s(oul is at) r(est), [came] and said,  
intentionally and will[ingly ...]  
[...]  
in the manner of Jewish men, who [nou]rish, [su]stain, and [...]
and honor their wives faithfully. And this Ghāliya [...] listened to him (accepted his proposal)  
and consented to be married to him and to esteem and honor him, to attend and to serve [him in the manner of]  
respectable women, the daughters of Israel, who esteem, honor, attend, and serve  
their husbands in purity and cleanness. This Ghāliya appointed her brother, Ḥalfōn b. Musā[fir],  
to be her agent for the receipt of her qiddush (betrothal gift) from the hands of this Ḥalfōn b. Aaron.  
And she willingly consented to all he does concerning her match and what he stipulates on behalf of her and as an obligation upon her. And there testified  
to her two witnesses, who are acquainted with her. The mohar that this Ḥalfōn, the groom, set  
for this Ghāliya, the bride, is twelve dinars. Two dinars he gave as a first payment [...]; and there remain  
incumbent upon him ten perfect, weighed dinars, of the dinars of the state, delayed as a debt upon him,  
sound and firm. She has no right to claim of them one peruṭa as long as he  
is alive and she is under his jurisdiction and he fulfills her three needs. But if he hates her without  
any misconduct (on her part) and does not fulfill her three needs, he shall pay them to her, viz. the balance of her mohar, of
twelve dinars, and release her with a bill of divorce. And these are what she brought with her from the Merciful and from 
the house of her fathers: a pair of gold earrings—2 dinars, a wrap—2  dinars, a coat made of different materials—
¼ dinar, a skullcap—1 dinar, a skullcap and a gown—2 dinars, a "half-garment" and a slip—  
2 dinars, a wrap— 1 ½ dinars, three Ṭabarī cushions and a pair of ʿAbbadānī mats—  
1 dinar, a chest and a bench—1 dinar, a basin and a pitcher—1 dinar, a lamp— 
2 dinars, and gold—2 dinars. The sum total is 16 dinars and ½ 
dinar and ¼ dinar. And they are for her and her son after her. And if she passes away without leaving  
sons or daughters by him, what remains will be divided into two equal portions.  
One portion will be acquired by her husband, and the other portion will return to the house of her fathers. And with this  
understanding, the two sides stipulated and agreed between themselves concerning hate and love  
and life and death and all the stipulations of the Torah and the court stipulations from beginning to end. And they took  
upon themselves the obligation of this marriage contract according to the stringencies of all valid documents,  
verified in court, not like promises and not like formularies. And we performed with them  
a complete qinyan, with an implement fit for doing so, on all that is written and specified  
above. This marriage contract is established, verified, and trustworthy wherever it is produced and read,  
whether according to the laws of the nations of the world or according to the statutes of our lords, the sages. May they build and prosper.
Amram ha-Kohen b. R. Aaron (may his) e(nd be) g(ood). Abraham b. R. Joshua he-ḥaver (who) r(ests in) E(den).  
Japheth b. Abraham b. Siman-Tav (may his) e(nd be)g(ood). Samuel b. R. Nathan m(ay his) s(oul be) b(ound) i(n the bundle of) l(ife).
Amram he-ḥaver b. Ṣedaqa (who) r(ests in) E(den).

source: Mordechai Akiva Friedman, Jewish Marriage in Palestine: A Cairo Geniza Study (1980), vol. 2 (The Ketubba Texts).
content:
By Your name, our Creator. May they build and prosper, groom and bride.
On the fifth day of the week, which is the twenty-first of the month of Kislev, the second year of the sabbatical cycle, that is year 4[825]
A. M., in Ramle, which is adjacent to Lod of Judea. "I, Yeshuʿa b. Joseph (who) r(ests in) E(den), declare intentional[ly, willingly]
and of my own choice to take as my wife, you Berukha daughter of Ṣedaqa, with a mohar of 200 silver zuz, as has been fixed by [our] lords
the sages to give to the virgins, the daughters of Israel. And I will nourish, provide for, esteem and honor her in the manner of proper Jewish
m[en], who nourish, esteem and honor their wives, faithfully." And willingly
this Berukha, the bride, the virgin, the divorcee, took upon herself and became to this Yeshuʿa, the groom, a wife and the mother of children, with the [intention]
that she will serve ("stand before" him attend him in purity and cleanness. And this Berukha appointed Asad b. Mufarrij as (her)
agent, to care for her affair--with (in the presence of) two valid witnesses who were acquainted with her. And Ṣedaqa b. Ṣalaḥ, Ṣāʿid [ha-Kohen b.]
Eli performed a qinyan with her. And this Asad received for her three silver rings. And the two of them agreed to add to the mohar of the Torah eig[ht]
dinars. Of these he advanced two dinars; he received them from his hand in our presence. And there remain incumbent upon him six dinars, as a debt, sound and established.
And these are what she brought in: a slip, two slips, a skullcap, a qhite wimple, a lamp, a pad--five dinar[s and one third dinar.]
And she also brought in an upper story in the alley of al-Krʾh--a sitting hall, that is one half of the house, mixed, not divided, and all its rights, including the kitch[en],
and the toilet, and half of a well of salty water, for twenty-five dinars. The total of what she brought in is thirty and one dinars.
And this half house is what she inh[erited] from her father Ṣedaqa. And this Yeshuʿa undertook the responsibility of this ketubba and all the court stipulations
from beginning to end. And we performed with this Yeshuʿa a complete qinyan, as prescribed by law, with a proper implement. And they stipulated that her mother Ḥisān has the right
to dwell with them in the house. Sound and established, according to the law of Moses and Israel. In good order. 
Faraj b. Abraham (whose) s(oul is at) r(est). Ṣedaqa b. Yeshuʿa he-ḥaver (who) r(ests in) E(den).
Ṣedaqa b. Ṣalaḥ (may his) e(nd be) g(ood). Ṣāʿid ha-Kohen b. Eli (who) r(ests in) [E(den)].
Elijah ha-Kohen, called by the majesty of the Lord, the Head of the Academy, b. Gaon (may the) m(emory of the) p(ious) b(e for a blessing).

source: Mordechai Akiva Friedman, Jewish Marriage in Palestine: A Cairo Geniza Study (1980), vol. 2 (The Ketubba Texts).

By the name of the Lord. May we prosper in what we do. They built and prospered. The elders of Judea build and prosper.
On the fifth day (of the week), in the month of Av, sixteen days therein, year 4705
A.M., in the town Qugandim(a), which is on the river of Egypt, this marriage deed was written. “I, Hillel b. Joseph
(whose) s(oul is at) r(est) declare, intentionally and of my own choice, to take this Mubāraka, the virgin, the bride, daughter of Abraham,
(may his) e(nd be) g(ood), to be my wife, to take her in qiddushin, and (for her) to attend me in purity and modesty, in cleanness and sanctity,
As the modest and respectable daughters of Israel (do) with their husbands, in sanctity.” He undertook, this Hillel
b. Joseph (whose) s(oul is at) r(est) to nourish, provide for, clothe and cover, esteem, honor this Mubāraka, the virgin,
The bride, daughter of Abraham, (may his) e(nd be) g(ood), as the sons of Israel who conduct themselves with their wives in the manner of Jewish men. This
Hillel b. Joseph, the groom, betrothed (qiddesh) this Mubāraka daughter of Abraham, the virgin, the bride, with six gold pieces.
Of them he gave her two full gold pieces at the time of the betrothal (qiddush), and there remain “on his neck” four
\\”Israelite”// gold pieces. Isaac b. Yeshuʿa (whose) s(oul is at) r(est) her agent, received payment. And she consented to all that he do[es] in her affair. This
Isaac b. Yeshuʿa took upon himself the agency with (in the presence of) two trustworthy witnesses, by her [in]structions,
from beginning to end. They built and prospered.
This is what she brought in with her: a white mantle and a white gown–4 dinars, a sleeping mat and a quilt–2 dinars,
A red scarf and two headdresses–1 dinar, two pillows–1 dinar, a table and all that goes with it–eight
and ⅓ dinar. The total of what she brought in with her is 16 ⅓ dinars.
Ḥur ha-Kohen b. Abraham, (may his) e(nd be) g(ood), witness. I, Samuel b. Joseph, witness.
Joseph b. Ṣedaqa ha-Levi, witness. I, Solomon b. Faraj, witness.
I, Jacob b. Binyām, witness. ⟦Hiba b. I, Sam⟧ Samue[l] b. Hiba.
Amram b. Abraham, witness. Khalaf b. Bishr, witness.
Mevorakh b. Najm, witness. Shemarya b. Naʿmān, witness.
Hillel b. Joseph, the groom, witness. I, Isaac b. Faraj, witness.

source: Mordechai Akiva Friedman, Jewish Marriage in Palestine: A Cairo Geniza Study (1980), vol. 2 (The Ketubba Texts).
content:
verso
By the name of the Lord. May we prosper in what we do. In a good sign.  
On day X of the week, which is month X, of the year four thousand,
eight hundred and such and such A.M., which is year
1,393 of the era of documents, 
and from the destruction of the Temple, one thousand and such and such years—may the Merciful rebuild it in our day  
and in the days of all Israel—(this) marriage contract was written, here, in place  
X, which is situated by locality X: R. X son of X said to Miss
X daughter of X, the virgin, "Be my wife, according to the law of Moses, the prophet, and Israel,  
the chosen. And I will serve, feed, support, sustain, maintain,
and honor you, in the manner of Jewish men, who feed, <clothe,> and esteem
their wives, faithfully. And I will give you the value of the beauty of your virginity  
in a ketubba of 200 zuz, which Moses instructed to give to the daughters  
of Israel, the virgins." Similarly responded X, the bride, and declared
and undertook to serve, attend, esteem and honor
R. X , the groom, according to the norms of women, the daughters of Israel, who serve 
attend, esteem, and honor their husbands, in purity and cleanness.  
"And I, X, the groom, willingly have released (hereby release) X , the virgin, the bride, of all  
vows, bonds, oaths, and vows by ḥerem, which are (will be) upon her from this
day until the time that she will be under my jurisdiction. They are all forgiven and pardoned  
by the Merciful and by me, I, X , her husband, as it is written, 'Her husband 
has annulled them, and the Lord will forgive her.' " And R. X, the groom, said, "This, the mohar of your virginity
is so much the advanced payment and so much the delayed payment.” And these are the total  
of the articles which she brought in to him with herself from her  father's house to her husband's house:  
clothing, worn clothing, and jewelry, evaluated at such and such. And thus said  
R. X , the groom: "I undertake the responsibility for this marriage contract, on myself and on  
my heirs after me. And male children that you may have by me shall inherit  
your ketubba money beyond their share with their brothers from another  
wi[fe]. And female children that you may have by me (they) shall dwell in my [ho]me  
and shall be sustained from my property until they are married to Jewish men,  
the children of Israel. And if you are taken captive, I will ransom you with my possessions,  
exclusive of your ketubba money; and I will take you back. And I will not wron[g] you concerning  
this. And if I go to my eternal home before you, you shall dwell
in my house and be supported from my estate for the [d]uration of your widowhood  
or until you choose to tell my heirs to pay to you the money 
of your ketubba . And if you go to your eternal home bef[or]e me, I will
attend to your shrouds and to your burial; and I shall inherit you." And [they] likewise stipulated]  
between themselves the condition(s) of... fel[lows](?). And if R. X, the groom, ha[tes]  
[X, the bride, and does not desire] her partnership and wants to sep[arate]

[On the fifth day,] in the month of Kislev, twelve days therein, in the th[ird] year [of the sabbatical cycle, which is year four thousand,]
[seven hundred and] eighty-four A.M., in the city of [Tyre, was written]  
[this marriage [contact]: Nathan ha-Kohen of Safed b. Solomon, (may his) e(nd be) g(ood), b.'[...], came [and said, "Intentionally, willingly,]  
[voluntarily, and] of my own choice, and not being coerced, not constrained, and not pressed, [... rather]  
[... with] full [senses] and clear speech, I desire, of my own will, to marry [my] betrothed [...]  
[Rachel daughter of...] the [ḥa]zzan, (may his) e(nd be) g(ood), son of our master Abraham the ḥazzan, (whose) s(oul is at) r(est), that I might bri[ng] her into my house, so that she will be [my wife ... on condition]  
[that I hono]r her, feed her, sustain her, esteem [her], as all [... in the  man]ner of dece[nt Jewish] men, [who...]  
[... fa]ithfully. I have fixed as an obligation for her incumbent upon me qidd[ushin...] fifty dinar[s...]  
[... and fi]ve dinars, fully weighed, pure go[ld ... o]f which five fully weighed (coins) are [the] adv[anced payment. And there remain incumbent upon me]  
[...] a strong firm [debt]." And [this] l[a]dy Rachel, the virgin, listened to him (accepted his proposal)] and took upon [herself to be married]  
[to him ...] according to the laws of Moses and Israel. And she  undertook to honor, esteem, attend and [serve him ... in the manner of]  
[dece]nt [women], the daughters of Israel, who attend and serve their husbands in purity and san[ctity....]  
[And this girl] has reached her majority, with physical signs of maturity. She has attained puberty and is in her own jurisdiction. She has appointed [our] ma[ster ...]  
[... to b]e her agent for the business of her mohar. And she consented to all that he do[es.... There testified to her before us]
[two] fit [witnesses] who are acquainted with her—and for the receipt of her qiddush money. And this our master [...] acknowledged
[that he had received] the [adv]anced payment of her mohar, five dinars, the qiddush money of this Rachel, his daughter, and [...]
[...] And he (the groom) brought her into his home and took her in complete qiddushin, by money, by writ, and by [intercourse ...] 
[... trustworthy, pious. And there remain incumbent upon him twenty fully weighed, pure gold dinars, of the dinar[s of the state ...]
[...as the del]ayed payment, against him. She has no right to claim them from him as long as he is alive [and she is under]
[his jurisdiction], well-off, not hungry, nor thirsty. And these are what this Rachel brought in from the house [of her fathers ...]
[to the house of] her [hus]band: gold bracelets known as aswira—twelve d[inar]s, [a pa]ir of gold earrings [...]  
[...] two silver bangles—three dinars, silver anklets known as khalākhil—eight [dinars...]  
[...]—one dinar, a copper pail and a shallow drinking vessel—one  dinar, a short-cut shirt—two d[inars...]  
[... dinar]s, two colored shirts and a skullcap two dinars, three pillows  know[n as makhādd...]
[...]—one [di]nar, a shirt and two scarves—one dinar, a shirt—one  dinar, two larg[e] sheets—[...]  
[... dinar]s, three protective head coverings—one dinar, a colored skullcap and coat—two dinars, two skullcaps [...]  
[...] two [s]hirts and a skullcap—two dinars, a colored quilt coverlet—one dinar, a copper lamp [...]  
[These are wh]at this girl brought in from the Merciful and from the house of her fathers. They total for her to a number of fo[rty-...]
[dinar]s and one third dinar. And they are for her and for her son after her. If she passes from the world in her husband's life, [her son shall]
[acquire] whatever remains of these articles. And if, God forbid, she passes from the world without [children, half shall return to the house of]  
her [fathers.] And they stipulated between themselves concerning  hate and love and life and death—If this Natha[n, the groom, hates]
[this] Rachel, his wife, and does not desire her partnership—a gratuitous hatred, he shall pay her all that is wr[itten and specified in this]  
marriage [contract], completely. And if this Rachel, the bride, hates this Nathan, her husband, and does not desire his partnership, she shall]  
[los]e the delayed payment of her mohar and shall take what she brought in, and she shall not leave, except by the authorization of [the] cou[rt. "And if]  
[I go to] my eternal [h]ome before you, female children [that] you will have by me (they) shall dwell in my house and shall be [supported from my estate]  
[until] they are married to decent J[e]wish men. And you shall dwell in my house and shall be provided for from my estate [for the duration]  
of your [widowhoo]d, until my heirs choose to pa[y you] your ketub a [mo]ney." And he stipulated for her: "If you go mad, [...] 
[...] your ketubba money. And if you are taken captive, I will rans[om you] and I will return you to your city. And if you leave [the] w[orld before me,]  
male [children] that I shall have by you (they) shall inherit your ketubba money beyond their share which [they] shall inh[erit with]
[the]ir [brothers], which I may have from another wife"— and all the court stipulations from beginning to end. And th[is Nathan,]
[the groom,] acknowledged that he received in full all that is written  and specified in this marriage contract. And he said: ["I am] obligated to make payment,]  
[whether myself] or from my heirs who will remain after me. And all things that I possess and that I shall acquir[e, whether]
[mo]vables or real estate, all of them will be surety and guaranties for payment of this marriage contract."  
And the two sides [took upon] the[mselves] the responsibility and stringencies of this marriage contract according to the stringencies of val[id] deeds  
[verified in court. And with this understanding the two sides concluded and consented, willingly and [...]  
[not co]mpelled not restrained. And we performed with them a  complete, stringent qinyan, with an implement fit for doing this [for all]  
[that is] written [and specified above. [And they instructed the scribe to write] and the witnesses to testify....

On the fourth day (of the week), in the month of Nisan, fourteen days therein, the sixth year of the sabbatical cycle, which is y[ear f]our thousand,  
eight hundred and forty-three A.M., in the town of Damsīs, situated on the Nile river: Eli b. Aaron (whose) s(oul is at) r(est) \\the kohen//  [declared]
voluntarily, willingly, and of his own choice, not coerced, not distressed, not enticed, nor intoxicated to take this lady  
Ḥisān, the virgin and bride, daughter of m(aster) Jacob the kohen (whose) s(oul is at) r(est)—to esteem honor, nourish, provide for, and clothe [he]r, in the manner of Jewish  
men, who nourish, provide for, and clothe their wives, the daughters of Israel, in cleanness and purity. Similarly responded Ḥisān, the virgin and bride,
daughter of m(aster) Jacob, the kohen, who is at rest, that she would esteem, honor and attend him, in the manner of modest women, who esteem, honor, serve and attend  
their husbands, the sons of Israel, in purity and sanctity. And he effected her qiddushin with a cup of wine and a silver ring. And they fixed the mohar between them at thirty [dinars],  
comprised of ten dinars that are advanced and twenty full dinars, in royal coinage, that are delayed—after he had given her twenty-five [the mohar]  
of virgins, in silver zuz, in agreement with what the sages of Israel had expressed: "Not, less than two hundred is given for a virgin and one hundred for a widow." And the t[wo] sides  
agreed on this mohar. These are what she brought, in with her with her with the assistance of the Merciful: a pair of gold earrings–three dinars,  
a pair of bangles–three dinars, a pair of bracelets–two dinars, a white wimple–two dinars, two linen shirts–two dinars,
a shawl–one and a quarter dinars, a woman’s scarf and an Ashkelon headdress–one dinar, a mat–one dinar, seven c[ushions?]–one dinar, two skullcaps–
one dinar, a sleeping mat–one dinar, a pair of pants–one half dinar and necessities–one fourth dinar. The total of all [which] she brought in: [nine-]teen 
dinars. They will be for her and her son after her. This girl is of age and in her own jurisdiction. This girl, the bride, appointed Shela, the kohen, b. R.
Jacob, the kohen who is at rest, as her agent and to care for her affair, by the word of two witnesses who were acquainted with her. And [thes]e are their names: Aaron,
the elder, b. R. Barukh, (who) r(ests in) E(den), and Sason b. Eleazar, of Aleppo, r(emembered) for (good). Eli, the groom, \\the kohen// b. Aaron, (whose) s(oul is at) r(est), and Ḥisān, the virgin, the bride, daughter of Jacob, [the] kohen, agreed
to this writ and to its contents, after it had been read to them from beginning to end. And this writ is sound, firm, trustworthy, and verified
Whether according to the statutes of our lords, the sages, or according to the laws of the kingdoms. And we performed with them a complete qinyan with a fit implement. IN GOOD ORDER.

according to the custom of the small synagogue. They fixed the mohar between them at thirty gold pieces: twenty-five, the custom of the congregation and f[ive,]
an addition. He advanced at the time of this security seven gold pieces, and he shall pay to her three when he marries her. May he be built by her.
And twenty will be written "on his neck" as delayed. Moses b. Nissi, [Tāmma'js representative-guardian received for her the ring of security.  
She is in his jurisdiction, and he shall provide for her needs until the time of her marriage to him (i.e., to Hillel). This girl owns one of [two]
portions, in a compound known as the compound of Abū Yūsuf, in the building (qaṣr) in the street of the Jewish bathhouse, namely the  middle level apartments,
from what she inherited from her father. Their boundaries are: to the south, the apartments of Muʾmin and the apartments of the sons of Jeremiah; to the east, it is adjacent to the w[all of]  
the city; to the north, the apartments of Ibn Mus(a); and to the west, the exedra of the large courtyard, known as al-qaṣr. This por[tion,]
(one) of two portions, is with all its boundaries and exits and entrances, with all its rights, exposed and concealed, coming and going, between them....

[... when she is (still) under] his jurisdiction a division will be made of the land and what  
and what remains of her dowry into two equal portions. Half her husband will acquire,  
and half will return to the house of her fathers. And it is a monetary stipulation (and) is valid. And 
Manṣūr, this groom, acknowledged that he received in full all th[at] is written and specified  
above. And he said: "I am obligated to make payment, whether myself or from my heirs who will stand after me.  
And all things that I possess and that I shall acquire, whether real estate or movables
will be surety and guarantees for the payment of this marriage contract.” And they stipulated between themselves con-
-cerning hate and love and life and death and all the court stipulations from beginning
to end. And they also stipulated between themselves that Ḥaẓiyya would live in Tyre twelve  
months, and afterwards he will move her to the city of Akko, without delaying or deferring.
Further they stipulated between themselves: If m(aster) Nathan, her father, should happen to go to Akko, after
his daughter Ḥaẓiyya goes (there), he will live in this house, whether he is alone or his wife  
is with him and his children, whether to visit or to dwell (there) all his life, because on this condition he had given it to his daughter
Ḥaẓiyya; and he had imposed on her this stipulation. Manṣūr, her husband, obligated himself by it without (any) protest 
and without hesitating. And the two sides took upon themselves the security and stringency of this  
deed according to the strength and stringency of all valid deeds, verified in court
not like promises nor like formularies of documents. And with this understanding, the two sides concluded  
and consented, not being coerced nor compelled; and they told the scribe  
to write and the witnesses to testify. And we performed with them a complete, strict qinyan,  
with an implement fit for doing this, for all that is written and specified above. Valid,  
correct, and verified is this marriage contract wherever produced and read, whether 
according to the statutes of our lords the sages or according to the laws of the gentiles. May he build and prosper. In good order.
The papers are three. There is written on the joint, perpendicularly, in two places "true and corr[ect]."
And the number of lines is ninety-four. Strong and firm.
"I have read this copy and have transcribed the testimony which is in the ketubba. And it is  
correct,” written by Joseph ha-Levi b. R. Manasseh (who) r(ests in) E(den). 
Mevorakh b. Menahem (whose) s(oul is at) r(est).
Samuel b. R. Moses he-ḥaver (who) r(ests in) E(den).

[ ]אדאם אללה עזה פי יבמה וקע[ת] בין ידי
[אכוין אלכביר] מנ[הם גרצה פ]י אלמאל לא פי אליבמה לאן לה אמראה
[ואולאד לה] מנה[א ואכוה] אלצגיר עזב ליס לה אמראה //זוגה// וגרצה פי
[אלצביה ואלא]מואל וט[לב אלכ]ביר מע וסאיט סו אן יברטלו אלצגיר ד דנניר
[חתא ל]א [י]אכד אלצב[יה פל]ם יואפקהם אלצגיר עלי דלך אלא יקול לאכי[ה]
[אמ]א אן תאכד אלצביה או נאכדהא אנא פתאסף אלכביר עלי אלמאל
[א]ן לא יאכד מנה שי פקאל אנא נאכדהא והו גיר משתהי להא אלא רגבה
[פ]י אלמאל למא עלם אלצגיר אן שהוה אכיה וגרצה פי אלמאל אכתר מן אלצביה
[ס]בק ועשה מאמר ביבמתו קבל תמאם ג שהור אלעדה יפתינא סידנא
הל יתבת לה אלעקד ועלי אנה בתוך שלשה חדשים לקול אלקדמא ואם קדם
קטן זכה או לא יגוז פעלה אלא בעד תמאם ג שהור עדתהא ואן קאל אלכביר
אלאן אנא ניבמהא מע עלמנא אן גרצה פי אלמאל לא פי אלצביה נגוז לה דלך
ונבטל פעל אלצגיר לקולהם מצוה בגדול ליבם ואחרי ואוכד אן עקדהא
בעד תמאם //אל//ג שהור ונמצי פעלה יפתינא סידנא אלרייס אלגליל ואללה
יטול עמרה ויזידה עלמא ופהמא ושכרו מכופל מן השמים
[ג]עה שאלה זו לפנינו לשער הישיבה והתבוננו בה ולפי שהיא
בלשון הגרי צוינו לכתוב תשובתה בלשון הגרי אן כאן אלאמר
עלי מא סאלה אלסאיל בלא תגייר פאליבמה למן סבק ועשה
בה מאמר ושרח דלך אן אלסאיל סאל וקאל אן יבמה וקעת בין
אכוין אלכביר מנהם גרצה פי אלמאל לא פי אליבמה לאן לה זוגה
ואולאד ואלצגיר גרצוה פי אלצביה ואלמאל אד הו עזב וליס לה
זוגה וטלב אלכביר מע וסאיט סו אן יברטל אלצגיר ד דנאניר חתא לא
יאכד אלגואב יגב אן יעלם אלסאיל אן אללה חרם עלינא אשת
אח באסתתנא אן כאן לה ולד והו מא דוון פי משנה תורה
פי כי ישבו אחים פקול אלכתאב יבמה יבוא עליה לא יכלו אמרה
מן אחד ק[ס]מין אמא אן יכון אסם לשכץ מעיין והו אלכביר
אלאכואן או אסם ללגנס אעני מן תקדם מנהם אכד פהו יבמה
[ ] קאלו רבותינו זל מצוה בגדול ליבם לא רצה מהלכין על
[כל האח]ין וקאלו איצא מצוה בגדול ליבם ואם קדם הקטן זכה

דרב נחמן אמ ליה פתח פתוח מצאתי אמ להו רב נחמן אסבוה כופרי
מברכתא חביטא ליה והא רב נחמן דאמ מהימן מהימן ומנסבינן
ליה כופרי רב אחאי משני כאן בבחור כאן בנשוי ומן הדא אלקול
נסתפיד אנה אנמא האמינוהו חכמ פי קדר אלתקנה אלדי תקנו והו מנה
מאתים פאמא מא כתב להא הו עלי נפסה באכתיארה לא האמינוהו
חכמים וחכמהא חכם אלאילונית אלדי קאלו אין לה כתובה ואם מתחלה
נשאה לשם אילונית יש לה כתובה ונשים שאמרו חכמ אין להן כתובה
כגון ממאנת וחברותיה שאין להן מנה מאתים אבל תוספת יש להן
ועלי קולך אן אדעי רגל אנה בעל ולא מצא בתולים יגב אן
תעלם אן בין טענת דמים ובין טענת פתח פתוח פרק כביר כמא
קאלו פי אלפרק אלאכר החרשת והשוטה והבוגרת ומוכת עץ אין להם
טענת בתולים וסאלו ובוגרת אין לה טענת בתולים והאמ רב בוגרת
נותנין לה לילה הראשון ואגאבו או דקא טעין פתח פתוח הכי נמי הכא

מעשה שהיה לפנינו אנו בית דין והחות[י]ם עדותם למטה כן הוה בחדש כסליו
דשנת אלפא וארבע מאה וחמשין ותלתא שנין לשטרות בפסטאט מצרים דעל
נילוס נהרא מותבה רשותיה דאדוננו שמואל הנגיד הגדול נגיד ישראל ויהודה
יהי שמו לעולם חצר אלינא אלש[י]ך אבו אלברכאת אלמחלי אלכרזי מ ור ברכות הזקן
בן מר ור סעדיה הזקן נע וקאל לנא אנני כנת קד זהקת עלי רוחי וגרת מני אימאן
לא אבד אמא אתזווג וכנת קד אתפקת אנא ואהלי זוגתי אלתי הי אלאן פי עצמתי
//נעמה אבנה אבו נצר// אנהא תטלק לי אלזיגה לאני אע[ר]צת עליהא אכד מוהרהא ואלאנפצאל מנהא
פלם תאתר הי דלך בל קד דכלת להא תחת אלשרוט אלדי אלתמסתהא מני
והו אני לא אותר עליהא אלזוגה אלתי אתצל אליהא בל אואסי בינהם פי אלמבית
ואלנפקה ואלכסוה ולא אפצל ענהא בשי בל יכון אלמבית לילה בלילה פי אלחול
ואלסבת ואלעיד עלי סוא בינהם וכדלך אלנפקה ואלכסוה ואן רזקת מן אלזוגה
אלגדידה אלדי אתצל בהא ולד דכר או אנתי ותופית אנא בעד דלך לם יכון לה
עלי נעמה אבנה אבו נצר זוגתי הדה ולא לאחד ממן יסתחק מנה עליהא
חכם ולא מטאלבה ולא ימין אלבתה ואפילו חרם סתם אד קד געלתהא
נאמנת עלי ועל כל יורשי אחרי בדיבורה בביתה ובכתובתה //ובכל מיני תשמישתה// בכל ועל הכל
ודפעת ענהא סאיר צנוף אלאימאן כפיפהא ותקילהא ואפילו חרם סתם ועל
ידי גלגול וכדלך איצא לי ענדהא פי אלבית חויגאת אנא אתבתהא ולהא פיהא
שרוט מהמא אנא בחיים ואן קצי עלי אלמחתום כאנת נאמנת אלנאמנות
אלכאמלה אלמדכורה לעיל פי מא תקולה פיהא ומהמא אנא פי קיד אלחיאה
ותזווגת וכרהת זוגתי דא אלמקאם מעי כאן עלי אן אקים במוכרהא גמיעה
ואטלאק סראחהא ולא אעיקהא וכאן לבית דין אן לם אקים במוכרהא אן
יביע הדה אלאעלאק גמיעהא ותסלם אליהא מן מוכרהא ואקים להא אנא
במא יתבקא להא מן מוכרהא ואלבליות אלדי להא פאשהדו עלי בדלך
ואקנו מני עליה והדא תבת אלחואיג קגקין ומגסל ומרפע וגטאה ותלאתה
זבאדי פצה ומדבה אלגמיע פצה וכזאנה דולאביה כבירה ובסאטין כבאר
ובסאטין צגאר מע אלה אלבית וחין אדן אקנינא מן מ ברכות הזקן בן מ סעדיה
הזקן נע לנעמה אבנה אבו נצר [ד]א קנין גמור חמור בכלי הכשר לקנות בו
מעכשיו על כל מה דכתיב ומפרש לעילא ברצונו בלי אונס כלל בביטול
כל מודעין ותנאין על כל מה דכתיב ומפרש לעילא ושהדותא דא כתבנא
וחתמנא למיהוי לזכו לאחר היום שריר וקיים תלוי בין שיטי נעמה אבנה אבו
נצר ותלוי ובכל מיני תשמישתה והכל קיים יוסה הלוי בר יפת נע

למא כאן יום אלאחד א[ל]תאלת מחדש [ ]מצרים דעל נילוס
נהרא מותבה רשותיה דהדרת יקרת[ ]רבינו אדונינו גאונינו
נתנאל הלוי רכב ישראל ופרשיו יחיד הדור [אב המ]שרה ר[אש הי]שיבה שלגולה יהי שמו
לעולם כן הוה חצר אלינא מנצור בן מכארם אלבלביסי נע ואבו נצר בן אבו סעיד דידיע
בן אבנה עתיב וקאל לנא מנצור אלמדכור אעלמו אנני קד אלתמסת אלזואג במעאלי
אבנה אבו אלפכר דידיע בן אלמצמודי נע אכת אבו נצר אלמדכור מן אמה וקד תקרר
ביני ובין אבו נצר אלמדכור אן יכון מקדם אכתה אלמדכורה דינארין במתנה מעת
הכינוס ואן יכון מוכרהא כמסה עשר דינארא מחקקה ואן יכון סכנהא ב[מס]כן א[כר]
כארגא ען אלמסכן אלתי תסכן פיה זוגתי עמאים אלתי הי אלאן פי עצמתי וא[ן לא]
אתזוג עלי מעאלי אלמדכורה זוגה אכרי כארגא ען זוגתי עמאים אבנה כ[ ]
אלמדכורה לעיל ואן תכון מלאח אבנתי דירא עם מעאלי אלמדכורה בדירה
חדא ואכלא עמה על פתורא חד ואעתרף בין ידינא אבו נצר אלמדכור
אעתראפא תאמא אנה קבץ ותסלם מן מנצור אלמדכור דינארא ואחדא
מן גמלה אלדינארין אלתי תקררת בינה ובין מנצור אלמדכור ען מקדם
אכתה מעאלי אלמדכורה חסב מא שרח לעיל ואקנינא מן מנצור אלמדכור
קנין גמור חמור בלפט מעכשיו ברצונו בלי אונס כלל בביטול כל מודעין
ותנאין אנה קד אוהב לאבו נצר אלמדכור מעכשיו אלדינאר אלמדכור במתנה
גמורה מעכשיו גלויה ומפורסמת מתנה חתיכא חליטא שרירא וקיימא
ואקנינא מן מנצור אלמדכור איצא קנין שלם בלפט מעכשיו אן ענדה ופי קבלה
ודמתה ודרכה וכאלץ מאלה בתורת חוב והודאה גמורה מן אלעין אלגיד אל
דינארא ואחדא מצריא מצאפא ללדינאר אלדי תסלמה מנה חסב מא שרח ל[עי]ל
יקום לה מנצור אלמדכור בדלך מתי סאפרת מעאלי אלמדכורה אלי בלביס ותמנע
מנצור אלמדכור מן //אל//זואג בהא בעד מציהא אלי בלביס או מתי פסך שי מן אלשרוט אלתי
תקררת בינהמא לעיל או מתי ראם מנצור אן יתזיד שרוט עלי מעאלי אלמדכורה
כארגא ען אלשרוט אלתי תקררת בינהמא לעיל ואלדינאר אלדי [או]הבה מנצור אלמדכור
לאבו נצר אלמדכור עלי שרט אן תמצי מעאלי אלמדכורה אלי בלביס ולא תתמנע מן אלזואג
למנצור אלמדכור ואמא מתי תמנעת מעאלי אלמדכורה מן אלמצי אלי בלביס או מצאת
אלי בלביס ותמנעת מן אלזואג למנצור אלמדכור או פסכת שי מן אלשרוט אלתי
תקררת בינהמא לעיל כאן עלי אבו נצר אלמדכור אן יקום למנצור אלמדכור מעכשיו

הכהן הזקן נע אלזיגה במצר וכאן לה זוגה במדינה דמשק ללעדר אלדי דכרהוהו אן אלמלכות
יהדרה אל ליס תטלק לה כדמה חתי יכון לה זוגה פי אלדיאר יעוד אליהא וכנא עארפין דלך ואן אל
מנהג פי מצר לא תטלק לאחד זיגה ולה זוג[ה] אכרי אלא ען אכתיארהא ואןכאנת פי גיר אלדיאר
אן יחצר מוכרהא ויודע אלי אן יתקרר [א]מרה מע אלקדימה עלי אי וגה כאן פאעלמנא אבו יעקוב
יוסף אלכהן [[אלסקלי]] בדלך ואלזמנאה באחצאר מוכרהא אלדי דכר אנה כמסין דינאר פאחצר אלי
ענדנא שאהדין אתנין ושהדא אן אבו יעקוב יוסף אלכהן סלם לסת אלגמאל בת רבנא יוסף השר
הנכבד נע בעד צחה אלמערפה בהא ולבעלהא אלשיך אבו יעקוב //רבנא// יוסף התרגמן הנכבד בן
רבנא אבון השר הנכבד בעודו זל כמסון דינארא ואזנה מצרייה וצארת ענדהמאבודאעה
בית דין מוקופה למוכר זוגה רבנא יוסף הכהן דנן אלתי בדמשק אלי אן יצל מן מגלס אלחכם
מן דמשק מא יברי רבנא יוסף הכהן דנן מן דלך או מא יוגב אכדהא מן אלמודע למסתחקהא
ואנהם אקניא מן סת אלגמאל דא קנין גמור חמור בכלי הכשר לקנות בו מעכשיו בביטול כל
מודעין ותנאין אנהא קד שעבדת אלמלך אלדי להא פי אלגזירה עלי הדהאלכמסין דינאר אי וקת
אלתמסהא בית דין מנהא ואקניא איצה [[באלרצא]] מן רבנא יוסף התרגמן בעלהא דנן באלרצא
בדלך ואן כל מנהמא רבנא יוסף דנן וזוגתה מוכוד בהדה אלכמסון דינאראלחאצר באלגאיב
ואלמוסר באלמעסר ואלחי באלמיית וחין אדן אטלקנא לה אלזוגייה ומה דהוה קדמנא כתבנא
וחתמנא למיהוי לזכו יש טרטוש על באלרצא וקיים ותלי ביני שיטי רבנא והכל שריר ובריר וקיים
בעד דלך נקלנא אנן בית דין אלכמסין דינאר אלמדכורה מן תחת יד רבנא יוסף התרגמן דנן אלי
אלשיך אבו עמראן רבנא משה בן רבנא מנשה הזקן נע ודיעה לבית דין אלי אןיצל מן דמשק מא
יכלץ יוסף הכהן דנן ממא כתב עליה לעיל וכתב עלי אלשיך אבו עמראן דנןבאלכמסין דינאר

ותשועת צדיקים מיי מעוזם בעת צרה
אל מושב הדרת יקרת צפירת תפארת מרנו ורבנו נשיא
אלהים בתוכנו נסים הדיין המופלא החכם המעולה תפארת
החברים ישמרו צורו וינצרו יוצרו רעה לא תבוא אליו
ונגע ומחלה בל יקרבו באוהליו ייטיב אחריתו מראשיתו
מאת עבדו בן אמתו שלמה המלמד ברבי אליה הדיין סט
אלמשתאק אלי כדמתה אלמתאסף עלי אלפאית מן
מלאחצתה פאללה יגעלה לשם ולתהלה ויכון לה עונא
וסנדא לאנה אלמסאעד לאוליאה אלואתק לאתקיאה יתבת
פיה אלתירא כיאתך אני אלתשתע כיאני אלהיך אמצתיך
אף עזרתיך אף תמכתיך בימין צדקי אמן נצח סלה
וינהי אליה בעד אלסלאם אן סיידנא גאוננו אדוננו נגידנו
אברהם האור הבהיר והכוכב המזהיר יהי [שמ]ו לעולם
במאמר אלהי עולם כאן קד כתב לסיידנא שצ רקעה גואב
רקעתה פי מעני אבי מנצור בן אבי אלכיר צאמן סנהור ואמר
באן לא יזוגה אחד אלא בעד ופא מווכר זוגתה ואכד אלשיך
חסאן וכאלה בידה ומעשה בית דין בכט אלדיין אלאגל רבנו יהודה
בן אלנאמן זצל ומצי בחית אנה יגי מן ענד אלמולי גואב אלי
סיידנא אלנגיד יגביה בורא הצבאות מעלתו פמא גא מן
ענד אלמולי גואב פרגע אמר באן יכתב ללמולי
כתאב שאפי בשרח חאלהא ומא הי פיה מן אלשדאיד
ואלזאם אלשכץ באלוזן או יגי גואב סיידנא ובאללה עליך
יא מולאי וסיידי לא תגפל ען הדא אלאמר והודא הי צארכה
ללה תע והי תתנא פרג וגואב רקעתך אלשריפה אלי
סיידנא ירום הודו ויגדל כבודו פאן אלאמר מץ פיה
וקד כתב ללמולי [[הדה]] ורקה והי פי באטן הדה אלכדמה
באן תנגז אלקצה לאן עינהא וכאטרהא מנתצר גואב
אלמולא פלא יהמל אלקצה ואלאגר לה בין ידי אלבארי אללה
וולדהא איצא יקרא אלתורה והי מגתהדה פיה ותאלפה
בלא דרהם ועשית כחכמתיך ואתה כמאלך האלוהים
הוא ישכינך בטח שנ ורבצת ואין מחריד ושלומך

גדולת קדושת מרנו ורבנו נסים החבר היקר הנכבד
החכם המעולה ישמרו צורו וינצרו יוצרו רעה לא
תבוא אליו ונגע ומחלה אל יקרבו באוהליו ייטיב אחריתו
מראשיתו אנס וינהי אן למא כאן מן מדה חצרת
זוגה אבו מנצור בן אבי אלכיר צאמן סנהור בין ידי
סיידנא אדוננו גאוננו נגידנו נשיא אלים בתוכנו אברהם
האור הבהיר והכוכב המזהיר יגביה בורא הצבאות
מעלתו ויכון כסאו לעולם במאמר אלהי עולם ותצוורת
מן כון בעלהא יקצד אלזואג עליהא ואכרגת מסטור בכט
אלמולי אלדיין אלאגל רבנו יהודה שמרו צורו והו מעשה
בית דין אן מווכר הדה אלמראה אלמדכורה עליה
חוב גמור פתשכאת לסיידנא ירום הודו אנה קאצד
אלזואג פגאובהא סיידנא אן אחד מן אלמקדמין
מא יקדר יזוג אלמדכור לחית יופי אלמווכר פאמר
באן יכתב אלכתב ויוקע עליהא אלכט אלשריף פקבל
אמרה פלמא [[דכל]] חצר מן אזוגה דכלת בינ ידין
סיידנא ערפתה מא קד גרי נפד רקעה שריפה
אלי אלמולי אן יסייר וראה וינהיה ויאמרה אן
יופי אלמווכר אלדי עליה ואד לם יפעל דלך
פידכל אלי מקאם סיידנא ומושבו הגדול יירומם
יסמע כלאמה ויחכם בינהם פנפדת אלרקעה מן
מדה ולם יגי גואבהא פעז עלי סיידנא דלך
ואמר באן יכתב איצא הדא אלכתאב אלי אלמולי
אן יחרצה וינבהה פי אמר אלמדכור אן יופי
מא עליה וידכל תחת אואמרה ואד לם
יקבל דלך ואלא תכון פי אלמולי זריזות ופי מתל
הדה אלאשיא וחרידות לאן אדא אמר אלמקדם
שכץ מן ישראל באמר ולם יקבלה כאן דלך
עדוה עלי אלמקדם ואללום לה גאיה אללום וסיידנא
אלנגיד אבקאה אללה [[י]]אמר אלמולי אן יקף פי
הדה אלקצה לשם שמים ולא יתהאון פי חקוק
אלנאס ולא יהמל אמרהם ולא יגפל ען חקהם

אלשרעיה אצלא פיתפצל יהתם גאיה אלאהתמאם

אללה נור בין ידיה והלך לפניך צדקיך כבוד ייי
יאספיך וינהי אסתיחאשה לגלאלה ושדה
שוקה נחוה ותאלמה לפראק מתלה גמע אללה אל
שמל בה עלי אסר מא יכון בעד בלוגה מקצודה
וקצא חואיגה ויעלמה אן אלממלוך וולדה ומן
ענדה מחסובין מן גמלה עאילתה/ם/ ומא להם סוי
באב אלבארי סבחאנה ובאבהם הו ואלאך אלעזיז
גמע אללה שמלהם ולא אפרק בינה/ם/ אבדא וגעל להם
קדרה עלי פעל אלכיר ואבקאהם סנד לכל קאצדיה/ם/
ומא צאע להם אלי אלאן ענד ממלוכם שי למא
סאל תפצלה פי שרי אלוסט אלסקלי אוקף וגה אלופאה
קבל ספרה ואלמולי קד עלם צחיח אן ממלוכה
מא לה קדרה עלי אלגמלה ואנמא אלמולא יתפצל

גא רב המנונא קאל כנס מוציא אי אנה אן באדר

המנונא בקולה כנס אינו מוציא קאל רב //אשי// אלמעאר[ץ]
ומנאקץ עלי רב המנונא אנה אדא באדר ותזו[ג בהא לא]
נחוגה טלאקהא תם איצא אייד קול רב אשי זו[טי]

דלך אלחכם טלאקהא והו קולה תנא להו זוטי דבי
רב פאפי כדברי האומר כנס אינו מוציא תם
אחתאגו אלחכמים אן יסתכברו מן רב אשי אש
קולה הדא אן כאן הו הלכה קאטעה או קיאס
וחדס פלמא אסתנטקוה אלעלמא קאל להם
גמארא והלכה מקטוע עליהא קלתה ולם נקול

תפסיר דלך קאלת אלמשנה אלמתהום מע אלאמה

באן הדא לא יתזוג אחדאתהן ואן תזוג ופעל

ברננה לא מפקינן תפסיר דלך //צח// לא [[נזלם]] //נלזם// אלחכם
אלמתזוג ללמטלקה אלתי כאן חרמהא עלי בעלהא
באן יטלק מן גהת אן יוקאל אנה מא חרמהא

מעתוקה או גיר מגיירה קאל להא אנת מקדסא לי
בהדה אלקידושין אלתי דפעתהא לך [[עס]] אלסעה פי
חאלתך הדה ואנת אלסעה ממלוכה או ואנת עלי גיר
מדהב ישראל אדא תסלמת מנה תלך אלקידוסין
תם אנעתקת בעד דלך ואתגיירת לם //נחתאג// אלי קידושין
אכרי בל אלקידוסין אלאולה קד חאזתהא לה ותשבתת
בהא וצארת בתלך אלקידושין זוגתה בלא מחאלה ולא
צן ולא שך ועלי אנה סלם להא אלקידושין והי עלי מדהב

ולאחר שתשתחרירי תם דלך אלעקד בינהמא תמאם
אן כאמל ולא כאד אן ינפסך מנה שיא וכאנת זוגתה
והו זוגהא למא אנהם עליהם אלסלאם עללו דלך בעלה
קולהם מפני שלא הטעתו ולמא דכלת בעד דלך פי אל
מדהב וכאנת קד קבצת אלקידוסין מן אלאול אעני מן
קבל דכולהא פי אלמדהב צח אנהא תמת באלשרט

נחוגהא קידושין תאניה אלבתה פאן קאל קאיל

מעשה שהיה לפנינו אנו העדים הח[תומ]ים למטה בכתב הזה כי באו לפנינו
שתי אחיות שהיו מקודם היום גויות ערלות שם הגדולה פלונית ושם הקטנה
פל והתחננו אלינו ובכו בכי גדול ואמרו דעו רבותינו כי רצוננו להכנס בכלל
ישראל ולהיות מכם ולצאת מן הכלל שהיינו בו מקודם היום ושלא לעבוד
פסל ומסכה ואנו חפצים להכלל עמכם לעבוד את יי לבדו ולקבל עלינו [[כל]]
עול מלכות שמים ועול מצות כדרך כל בנות ישראל הכשרות הטהורות
וכששמענו אנו העדים דבריהם אמרנו להם דעו אחיותנו כי לא תוכלון
להיות עמנו בכלל ישראל לפי שקשה הוא ועלינו עול מלכות ואנו
בזויים שפלים מעוטים מכל העמים מעונים ואין אתם יכולין לשאת כל
אלה התנאים ומוטב לכם שתיהיו כוסתכם \\עם אחיכם ועמכם\\ ואם אתם חפצים כלום ואם
אין לאל ידכם עלינו לתת לכם מחסורכם ולעזור אתכם בכל יכלנו ובכל
מאודנו ויענו ויאמרו אנא רבותינו שאו למרום עיניכם [[עמנו]] \\בעבורינו\\
וחוסו עלינו כי לא [[יתכן לנו]] \\בכל עת\\ ימצאון עברים בזה המקום ועכשיו
שזימן הקבה כבר השתטחנו לפניכם ובקשנו מכם לעזור אותנו
על שאילתנו ועל בק[שתנו] ואין אנו חסירים כל דבר אשר בארץ
ועתה אחינו אם אין אתם עוזרים אותנו על זה הדבר אנו קובלים
עליכם לשמים וכששמענו זה הדבר פחדנו מדבריהם [שלא ימצא] אלהינו
עלינו עולה מן השמים והודענום עוד פעם אחרת שמעונו
אחיותינו יש עלינו הרבה מצות והרבה לאוין ומשמרות שלא תוכלון
אתם לשאת אותם והודענו דרכי הטהרה וה[טומאה וכי אסור להש]תחות [לאל]

content:
In the name of the Merciful One (Psalms 51:17). O Lord, open my lips and let my mouth declare Your praise (Psalms 51:17). You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, our God and the God of our forefathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob. You are the great, mighty and revered God, God on high, creator of the heavens and earth, our shield and the shield of our forefathers. Happy are those people who await your succour. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Shield of Abraham. Mercifully revive those who sleep in the ground and bring down the blessings of rain upon the earth. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Reviver of the Departed. Heavenly groups invest you with honour and those well-reared below clothe you with strength. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, the Holy God. Inform our minds with knowledge of what is right so that we stray not from your precepts. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Provider of Knowledge. Direct our hearts, those of a righteous nation who are always faithful, to perform your will. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, who takes pleasure in repentance. Wipe out of your memory the sins of our youth and forgive our iniquities. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, always ready to forgive. Remember [the deeds of the forefathers?], redeem their children and speedily restore us. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Redeemer of Israel. Swiftly heal the sickness of your people and bring about [full?] recovery. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Healer of his people Israel. Send down the purity [?] of rain this year and also a redeemer [?] to give thanks to your name. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Bringer of blessing to each year. May the scattered of your people fly back as a cloud, just as doves return to their dovecotes. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Gatherer of his scattered people, Israel. Deal justly, fairly and mercifully with your community. Deliver an upright judgement on the poor and the destitute. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Lover of Justice. Blot out the wayward from the book [?] of life and offer no satisfaction to those who challenge the faith. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Humbler of the Impious. Take account of the devoted intensity of the upright and bring joy to the hearts of those who sincerely attach themselves to you. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Security for the Righteous. Return in mercy to Jerusalem your city; may the throne of David be re-established within. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, God of David and Builder of Jerusalem. Hearken swiftly to our orderly prayer, our measured thought and our painful cry. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Heeder of Prayer. Turn again to your altar in our days so that we can make the offerings we owe and you can find favour in the Temple worship. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, the one whom we revere and worship. We give thanks to you, who are our God and the God of our forefathers; we bend the knee and prostrate ourselves before you, our Father and King, our Rock of Eternity, our Master of Peace, for all the loving and merciful kindnesses that you have bestowed on us and for what you have done for us and for our fathers before us. Those who seek you will praise you continually at all times, with lips, and tongue, and heart and gut. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, the Good One whom we must thank. May the Lord our God bless us. Take care of us and be gracious to us. Grant us your blessing of peace. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, Creator of Peace. You alone are the Lord. You made the heavens, the highest heavens, and all their host, the earth and everything upon it, the seas and everything in them. You keep them all alive, and the host of heaven prostrate themselves before You. You are the Lord God who chose Abram, who brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and changed his name to Abraham. Finding his heart true to you. (Nehemiah 9:5–8) . . . May you mercifully will it, our God and the God of our forefathers, that you . . . and inspire us, both us and all Israel [and draw us near?] to your reverence, as you wish, and to your Torah . . . and to perform your will, as You wish, amen. Lord, teach me to do Your will, for You are my God. Let Your gracious spirit lead me on level ground. For the sake of Your name, O Lord, preserve me; as You are beneficent, free me from distress. As You are faithful, put an end to my foes; destroy all my mortal enemies, for I am your servant. (Psalms 143:10–12) May the words of my mouth and the prayer of my heart be acceptable to You, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer. (Psalms 19:15)
[We thank you] for the miracles, rescue, and redemption that you performed for our forefathers through Mordechai and Esther in those days and at this time, when the wicked Haman arose against them and sought to destroy, kill and wipe out all the Jews from young to old, toddlers and women. You in your infinite mercy ruined his plan and nullified his intent, bringing retribution upon him and hanging him and his sons on the tree. So do perform for us, Lord our God, miracles and mighty deeds and we shall give thanks to your name, our king, selah. It is good to praise the Lord, to sing hymns to Your name, O Most High (Psalms 92:2). You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, the Good One whom we must thank.

source: Stefan C. Reif, Jewish Prayer Texts from the Cairo Genizah (2016).
content:
recto, left side
You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, and the universal sovereign. You are the one who performed miracles for our ancestors on these dates. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise and the universal sovereign. You have granted us a continuation of our lives and allowed us to reach this occasion.
Having drunk the contents of the qiddush cup, he washes his hands and recites the benediction: You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise and the universal sovereign. You have brought us holiness by your precepts and instructed us in the matter of hand-washing.
If the seder is being held 
verso, right side
on Saturday night, he recites the benediction: You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise and the universal sovereign, the Creator of fiery lights. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise and the universal sovereign. You created distinctions between different kinds of holiness, between holy Sabbath and festival, between the pure and impure, between the sea and dry land, between the upper waters and the lower waters, between the Jews and the non-Jews, between the holiness of the Sabbath and that of the festival. As the biblical verse states: You shall be holy to Me, for I the Lord am holy, and I have set you apart from other peoples to be Mine (Leviticus 20:26). He then takes some of the vegetables and recites the benediction: You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise and the universal sovereign, Creator of produce from the ground. Having dipped it, he eats it all, and then recites the benediction: You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise and the universal sovereign, the Creator of many forms of life for the benefit of all that he created. Praise to his universal existence.
He then takes the second qiddush cup and the most prominent member of the company, or his eldest son, begins to explain to them by asking, with the cup in his hand:
What is different about this night compared to all other nights? 
verso, left side
On all other nights, we do not dip our food even once, while tonight we are obligated to do so twice. On all other nights, we eat bread that has risen or fat matza bread, while tonight we eat only matza. On all other nights, we eat meat that is roasted, stewed or boiled, while tonight we used to eat only roast meat in the Temple. On all other nights, we eat all sorts of vegetables, while tonight we eat bitter-tasting ones. On all other nights, we eat in a sitting or reclining position, while tonight we all recline.
What is different about this night compared to all other nights? It was on this night that our ancestors left the land of Egypt. Our ancestors had been enslaved in the land of Egypt and subject to attacks by Pharaoh. The Egyptians distressed them and enslaved them, forcing them to do the kind of hard labour that they could not survive. Our ancestors prayed to the Holy One, who is to be praised, and he heard the sound of their cries and performed miracles for them and brought them out of there. When our ancestors left the land of Egypt, they took with them bread-dough that had not risen and they baked it on [baking boards] and they picked bitter-tasting plants and ate them [with the matza].

source: Stefan C. Reif, Jewish Prayer Texts from the Cairo Genizah (2016).
content: [We thank you] for the miracles, the mighty deeds, the acts of salvation, the battles, the redemption and the rescue that you performed for us and for our forefathers on these days. In the days of Mattathias, the High Priest, the Hasmonean, and his sons, when the kingdom of Yavam arose against your people with the aim of making them forget your Torah and transgress your express instructions, you stood up for them in your manifold mercies in their time of trouble, pleaded their cause, represented their case, took revenge for them, handing the mighty into the power of the weak, the many into the power of the few, the impure into the power of the pure, the insolent, the wicked into the power of the righteous and the insolent into the power of those who engage in Torah. You enhanced your great and holy reputation and brought about great salvation for your people Israel. Afterwards your people entered your chosen house, cleansed your palace, purified your sanctuary and kindled lights in your holy courtyards. They instituted eight days of praise and gratitude to your name. Just as you performed miracles for earlier generations, later ones, so do likewise for the later ones.

source: Stefan C. Reif, Jewish Prayer Texts from the Cairo Genizah (2016).
content:
Recto
Grace after Meals for Weekdays
You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, and the universal sovereign, creator of the world and moulder of mankind who prepares food for all his creatures, as the verse has it: You give it openhandedly, feeding every creature to its heart’s content (Psalms 145:16). You, Eternal one, are the essence of blessing who provides food for all. You created the land, you prepared the table, you provided us with Torah and covenant. We therefore thank you and praise your name, as the verse has it: When you have eaten your fill, give thanks to the Lord your God for the good land which He has given you (Deuteronomy 8:10). You, Eternal one, are the essence of blessing who gifted the land and the food. Rebuild your city, re-establish Jerusalem, and mercifully give your attention in our days to your Temple. Speedily restore your messianic kingdom to its place for our eyes are longing for you. Rebuild your holy city in our days, as the verses have it: The Lord rebuilds Jerusalem; He gathers in the exiles of Israel (Psalms 147:2); There I will make a horn sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for My anointed one (Psalms 132:17). You, Eternal one, are the essence of blessing, God of David and builder of Jerusalem. You, our Eternal God, are the essence of praise, and the universal sovereign, our Holy One, the Holy One [of Jacob], who is a goodly sovereign and confers goodness, who daily does good to us, who in the past, 
Verso
present and future is the bestower of grace, love and mercy, and of all goodness, as the verse has it: The Lord is good to all, and His mercy is upon all His works (Psalms 145:9). And as it is said in Scripture:, The Lord is good to those who trust in Him, to the one who seeks Him (Lamentations 3:25). And as it is said in Scripture: The Lord is good, a haven on a day of distress (Nahum 1:7). May what we have eaten satisfy us and may what we have left over be blessed. May what we have drunk, and what we shall drink, bring us health. May you be blessed by my God, amen. May you be succored by my God, amen. May you all be blessed.

content:
Recto
In [your] name, O Merci[ful].
Greetings from the four corners of the earth and favors from all sides, along with calm, quiet, serenity and other signs of security given by God, to [his] precious h[onor], g[reatness, and] h[oliness], [our] ma[ster] and t[eacher] Eli ha-Kohen the parnas and trustee of the court—may the Lord of Hosts protect you, envelop you with [His] wing, make your grey hairs resplendent with a crown of honor and a diadem of pride, grant you ripe fruit and a good end, and may your hope never be cut off—son of [his] h[onor], g[reatness, and] h[oliness], [our] ma[ster] and t[eacher] Ḥayyim ha-Kohen the mumḥe [expert judge—Ed.]—[may his] s[oul] r[est in peace].
I sent earlier letters to Your Excellency my master the Kohen the parnas and trustee of the court—may your Rock keep you and protect you from enemies—mentioning what I shall discuss here, namely, the situation about which I ask the Creator, praise Him, to make things turn out well in the end through His mercy. I explained to you also what was stated in the letter from our lord the head of the diaspora [rosh ha-gola]—may his name live forever—addressed to [our] ma[ster] Abraham the cantor—[may his] R[ock] k[eep him]—expressing his reliance upon me in all matters of service to the community, small and great. I also told you that the [ab]ove-[m]‌entione[d] can[t]or . . . came to me accompanied by a large number of the elders of the community—may God preserve them—and said: “You know that I am incapable of handling the duties that were thrust upon me. Neither I, nor the community, can do without your participating in public service [as] you have always done.”
However, I did not accede to their wishes one bit. In fact, I have resigned from all communal duties and from the service that I had accepted. I am not the least bit distressed over that, since I never derived any profit from my position, apart from the honor of serving our lord the head of the diaspora—may his name live forever. I earned only the hostility of a large number of people in the community because I am connected with his retinue. I have served him and been his faithful friend for a number of years in compliance with his command. I confess that I cleaved to him as steadfastly as any seeker of refuge and hope and, indeed, had put my hopes in that. Nonetheless, I ended up, as it were, unthanked, even though I believe that I have done no wrong and am free of guilt, as the people in the community well know. At any rate, I thank you for your favors. You—may God crush [your en]emies and protect you—will do what you must to restore proper order in your communities—may God adorn them with your long life and cheer them with your [continued] vitality. Perhaps thereby I will benefit along with the community. Whatever the Merci[ful] God decides to do will be for the best.
Now to my main reason for j[otting dow]n these lines. I wish to inform my m[a]‌ster the Kohen the parnas and trustee of the court—may God bless you and k[ee]p you—about the stature of the bearer of this letter. He is my master the elder Abū Sa‘d the wise and understanding one—may his Rock keep him and protect him from enemies—son of Phineas—[may he] r[est in] E[den]. He is one of the most valued of our Damascene coreligionists—may God cause them to increase. He is a man reared on Jewish learning and on good deeds. I feel personally obliged to provide for his needs by virtue of his goodness, modesty, and Jewish learning. In addition, he, I, and another scholarly relative of his have in common . . . , and love, being in awe of God.2 He has set out for Egypt on some affair of his. He has little experience in those parts, for this is his fi[r]st journey there.

Right margin
Please, my master the Kohen, keep an eye on him, watch over him, and hel[p]‌ him in whatever comes up in connection with his needs. He is carrying a receipt from the tax bureau attesting that he has pai[d t]he poll tax. If it is interpreted to his detriment, do not, my m[a]ster, ignore him in that matter. I will reckon everything you do for him as if done for me and will thank you and add this to your previous kindnesses towards me. May God in His mercy not release my master from doing this deed.
Greetings to you and to your son [our] ma[ster] and t[eacher] Ephraim,
Upper margin
sweet brother—may God cause him to be fruitful and multiply, and may he be great forever. My father and brother wish you both much peace and [the same to our] ma[ster] and t[eacher] Shemarya ha-Kohen—may God restore him to full health and increase his welfare and that of his sons forever. I ask that you give regards to my sister, to her son, and to his father—may God preserve them—from my father, from me, and from my brother. [Our] ma[ster] Hillel ha-Levi Elder of the Community wrote my master a number of letters, but has not had the favor of his good offices with our lord on his behalf. Therefore, do this for him out of your kindness, God willing.
May you be rewarded with peace and [me]rcy. [E]‌n[d] of Marḥeshvan, [1]405.
